He presents to the emergency department with his sister, who reports that he has been experiencing visual hallucinations and agitation since the morning. The patient admits to consuming a fifth of vodka daily but stopped drinking 18 hours ago.

Provider: Dr. Aisha Patel, MD

Visit Type: icu

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Acting strangely with agitation, tremulousness, and profuse diaphoresis

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns to the emergency department for the third time this year with similar symptoms, having previously presented in January 2020 with visual hallucinations and agitation and in May 2020 with agitation, disorientation, and tactile hallucinations. The patient presents with his sister, who reports that he has been acting strangely since he stopped drinking alcohol three days ago. The patient appears agitated, tremulous, and is profusely sweating. He is disoriented to time and place and reports visual hallucinations of small animals in the room. His sister confirms that he has a history of multiple attempts at alcohol cessation, but this is the first time he has experienced these symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Alcohol withdrawal delirium (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Delirium tremens (diagnosed 2020-05-15)
- Alcohol use disorder, severe
- Alcoholic cirrhosis
- Hypertension
- Thiamine deficiency
- Major depressive disorder
- Gastroesophageal reflux disease

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Appendectomy (age 22)

MEDICATIONS:

- Folic acid 1 mg PO daily
- Multivitamin 1 tablet PO daily
- Omeprazole 20 mg PO daily
- Amlodipine 5 mg PO daily

NKDA

- Mother: Hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus
- Sister: Generalized anxiety disorder (primary support person)

SOCIAL HISTORY:

VITAL SIGNS:
His vital signs are as follows: BP 160/100 mmHg, HR 120 bpm, Temp 38.9°C (102°F), RR 22 breaths/min

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Physical examination reveals an anxious-appearing male with increased psychomotor activity, dilated pupils, and a coarse tremor of the outstretched hands.

LABORATORY DATA:

Chloride: 102 mEq/L

BUN: 18 mg/dL
